header.title: API keys
header.description: Inbound credentials external partners use to call Atlas. Internal products do not go through here — they hold OIDC clients and call /v1/* with short-lived S2S tokens. Every rotation and revocation is recorded in Audit.

notice.externalUnwiredTitle: External keys are not wired into any authentication path yet — because there are no external partners today
notice.externalUnwiredDescription: The Atlas gateway accepts S2S OIDC tokens only on /v1/*, so an issued key cannot call the gateway today (TD-029). This is not an engineering gap: a third-party partner is not an OIDC client of the vxture IdP, a key is its only possible authentication method, and once a key is bound to a product_code the authorization model is already there. The one thing holding it back is that Atlas lives on the tailnet and atlas.vxture.com is reserved but unbound — what it waits on is a partner, not a sprint.
notice.retiredTitle: {count, plural, one {# retired Internal key} other {# retired Internal keys}} (all revoked)
notice.retiredDescription: The internal kind is gone: sibling products use OIDC S2S tokens, and handing them a long-lived shared secret would trade something stronger for something weaker. These old rows are kept rather than deleted — revoked is the terminal state of a dead credential, and deleting it would erase the fact that it was ever issued, along with its rotation history and audit trail. They never authenticated anything.

empty.noMatchDescription: Try a different keyword or type.

filters.cardsDisabledReason: Card view has been retired; use the list

bulk.selectedKeys: {count, plural, one {the selected key} other {the # selected keys}}
bulk.disableConsequence: While disabled, callers holding these keys are rejected until you enable them again. The keys themselves stay valid and can be re-enabled at any time.
bulk.doneDescription: Revoked keys and retired Internal keys are not affected by bulk actions.

revoke.consequence: Revoking is final: the key cannot be enabled or rotated again, and there is no “undo revoke”. The holder has to request a new one through the issue flow. To cut access temporarily, use “Disable” instead — that one is reversible.
revoke.doneDescription: Revoking is final; the holder has to request a new key.

delete.consequence: This removes the row only: name, owner, prefix and last-used time disappear. The issue / rotate / revoke trail is unaffected — it lives in the append-only Audit tables. A revoked key already rejects every call, so deleting it changes nothing for any caller; it only tidies the ledger.
delete.doneDescription: The row is gone; its issue, rotate and revoke trail remains in Audit.
delete.unsupportedTitle: This Atlas deployment has no delete endpoint yet
delete.unsupportedDescription: A revoked key already rejects every call, so nothing is functionally affected. This action becomes available once Atlas ships DELETE /capability/api-keys/:id.

issue.title: Issue API key (External)
issue.description: The secret is shown once, at issue time. After that it can only be rotated.
issue.externalOnlyTitle: External only: internal products do not use keys
issue.externalOnlyDescription: The sibling products (karda / arda / varda / runos) all hold OIDC clients and call /v1/* with 300-second S2S tokens, whose act.sub is the product identity the authorization tables recognise. Handing them a long-lived shared secret — stored on both sides, where whoever holds it is whoever it says — would add no capability at all; it would only replace something stronger with something weaker. That is why internal was removed rather than left unused.
issue.nameDescription: Calls are grouped under this name in logs and metering.
issue.ownerDescription: Whichever product_code the key is bound to, it becomes a product in the authorization tables — both authentication paths share one authorization model.
issue.expiresDescription: Leave empty for no expiry — it runs until revoked. Setting a date changes nothing about this row on its own: expiry is evaluated at read time, so the state column will read “Expired” while the row still says active. Actually withdrawing it still takes someone disabling or revoking it.

rotate.title: Rotate {name}
rotate.description: The old key stops working immediately. Until the holder switches to the new value every call returns 401 — agree on a cutover window first.

reveal.onlyChanceTitle: This is the only time you will see the secret
reveal.onlyChanceDescription: Once you close this you cannot view it again. A lost secret can only be rotated, never recovered. This key cannot call the Atlas gateway yet — /v1/* accepts S2S OIDC tokens only, and wiring waits on an external partner (see the note above). Do not hand it over as if it were ready to use.

metricCatalog.dialogDescription: The name and blurb are stored per metric key, so every product using this key shows the same name. Leave blank to remove the name and fall back to the key itself.

products.label: Affected products
products.hint: Pick from the product catalog; leave empty for a platform-wide notice. Starting the window puts these products under maintenance and holds new subscriptions; completing or cancelling restores them.
products.loadFailed: Could not load the product catalog, so affected products cannot be changed this time; retry and edit again.
products.lockedLive: Affected products are locked while the window is in progress; complete or cancel it to change them.

start.title: Start maintenance
start.effect: The website and console will show "Under maintenance" to everyone and stop new subscriptions; subscribed tenants are paused within a minute and their terms extended. It does not end by itself when the time comes — come back here and click "End maintenance".
start.endAtHint: Must be later than now. It only tells customers roughly when to expect the product back; nothing resumes automatically.
start.endAtInvalid: The expected end must be later than now
start.noteHint: Optional. Stored on the maintenance window, visible under Ops → Maintenance windows.

end.title: End maintenance for {target}?
end.consequence: The website and console become subscribable again immediately; paused subscriptions resume within a minute with their terms extended.

operatorNoticesPage.title: Operator notices
operatorNoticesPage.description: Messages for operators: product launches, new capabilities and change notices, plus what the platform broadcasts on its own — maintenance windows, job heartbeats, webhook dead letters. The three operator planes are staffed by different people; this is where the word gets across.

needsAction.title: Needs action
needsAction.loadFailedHint: Neither the unread count nor the needs-action list came back. Try again.
needsAction.summary: Sent to the runtime plane and still unread by you: {critical} critical, {warning} important, {info} info
needsAction.summaryNone: You have read every notice sent to the runtime plane.
needsAction.emptyUrgent: Nothing critical or important is unread.
needsAction.emptyUrgentWithInfo: Nothing critical or important is unread; {count} info notices are still unread and listed below.
needsAction.more: {total} critical or important notices are unread; the first {shown} are shown here, the rest are in the list below.

noMatch.title: No matching notices
noMatch.description: Try another severity, source or keyword.

empty.title: No notices yet
empty.description: Product launches, new capabilities and change notices are published here and reach all three operator planes; what the platform broadcasts on its own lands in this table too.

rowActions.label: Notice actions
rowActions.markReadOffPlane: This notice was not sent to the runtime plane, so there is no read state for you on it.
rowActions.markReadAlready: You have already read this one.

withdraw.consequence: Once withdrawn it disappears from all three planes and the people who read it will not see it again. Read receipts and the notice itself are kept on record, but it cannot be shown again — publishing it once more means creating a new one.

dialog.title: Publish an operator notice
dialog.description: Operators see this; customers do not. Customer-facing announcements are published from the operations plane.
dialog.identityHint: Title and body are what all three planes see directly.
dialog.bodyPlaceholder: Say what happened, who it affects, and whether anything needs doing
dialog.detailsHint: Sent to all three planes by default; narrow it only when one side is the only side that cares.
dialog.planesEmpty: With none selected nobody sees this notice — pick at least one
dialog.linkHint: A path inside the plane, so whoever receives it can go straight there.

operatorNoticesPage.truncated: {matched} notices match; only the first {shown} were fetched (per-request cap). Narrow the severity, source or keyword — paging only moves within what was fetched.
